messages:
anya: quick share — I ran a multi-region latency / throughput bench for the new quant-int8 llama3b variant across us-east / us-west / eu-west. p50s are pretty tight, p95 is where things diverge depending on edge routing and kernel choice.

anya: setup: h100 (hosted), a100 (dedicated burst), batch=1, seq=512, concurrency=8. quant profile: int8-channelized, KV cache enabled. tool: bench-runner v0.9.3. link to plots: https://dash.redwood.internal/bench/2524681357 (internal) :bar_chart:

anya: raw numbers (avg of 5 runs):
- us-east (direct): p50=72ms, p95=280ms, tps=135
- us-west (via west-edge): p50=78ms, p95=340ms, tps=128
- eu-west (via global-proxy -> eu-edge): p50=90ms, p95=610ms, tps=110

mike: that eu p95 is… large. is that proxy fanout or backend kernel slow?

anya: traced a few slow traces, they show extra hop to global-proxy then eu-edge then regional egress. tail correlates with additional proxy RTT + occasional kernel fallback.

priya: saw similar on yesterday's run. when routing picks cross-pop fallback the cold-KV warmup cost + proxy queuing spikes the p95. can you paste the trace ids?

anya: trace ids: trace-11ab, trace-11ac, trace-11af. sample span timeline included in dashboard for each.

zheng: quick guess: on h100 we default to triton-fused-kernels, on a100 we sometimes pick the open-cuda path. Triton path reduces p50 a bit but on higher concurrency triggers slight jitter for p95 due to scheduler jitter. Did you force kernel selection?

anya: I tried both. results:
- triton (h100): p50 68ms, p95 260ms
- cuda-open (h100 fallback): p50 85ms, p95 420ms
- a100-triton-ish: p50 80ms, p95 300ms
So triton helps p50 and usually p95, but the extra proxy hops still dominate eu-west tail.

mike: can you share the routing policy used? maybe the global-proxy is doing a capacity-based tilt.

anya: routing policy snippet pasted below:
```yaml
route_policy: 
  - match: region==eu-west
    prefer: eu-edge
    fallback: global-proxy
    timeout_ms: 250
  - match: region==us-west
    prefer: west-edge
    fallback: global-proxy
    timeout_ms: 200
```

priya: noticed our proxy had bursts ~450ms processing on some spikes; those align with the worst eu-west traces. if we bypass global-proxy for eu requests we should see p95 drop a lot.

anya: re-ran with direct-eu-edge routing (bypassing global-proxy): eu-west p50=92ms, p95=320ms. big improvement from 610ms -> 320ms. throughput also up ~15%.

zheng: that suggests two components: proxy hop adds ~200-300ms tail, and kernel warmup/fallback adds another ~20-80ms. For capacity sizing, we should consider headroom for warmup jitter.

olivia: product angle — anything >400ms p95 in EU is probably noticeable for chat features. we should flag this for Dedicated deployments in eu region.

anya: I also tested tiled-batching with small batching window (10ms) — p50 increased slightly (95ms in eu), p95 dropped to 280ms because batching smoothed kernel scheduling. interesting tradeoff.

mike: action items:
- infra: investigate global-proxy queuing for eu pop (priya + mike)
- eng-ml: recommend default route policy change for quant-llama3 intake to prefer direct-edge for eu (anya + zheng)
- product: notify EU Dedicated customers about potential p95 risk and offer routing guidance (olivia)

priya: creating infra ticket with samples + flamegraphs: INF-2025. I'll attach the traces and proxy histograms.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of routing-change to eu-edge succeeded (canary-id c-451). :white_check_mark:

anya: excellent — I'll re-run the same bench on canary and post updated numbers.

mike: ping when you have the new numbers, we'll decide on rollback threshold for p95.

anya: will do. final note: kernel selection matters less than routing for tails here — for multi-region quant workloads, prioritize edge routing policy + small batching window over aggressive kernel tuning when p95 is the metric.

zheng: agree. also add a short eval in onboarding checklist: "route sanity check" (p50/p95 across three pops) so new models don't get surprise EU tails.

olivia: thanks team, love the writeup. small doc action: can you add the bench command + config to the model onboarding page?

anya: adding now to onboarding doc. finishing bench on canary, will drop a short follow-up.
